title: Correct downward velocity
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the speed just before impact using energy or kinematics, obtaining 8 m/s.

title: Correct upward velocity
description: Essential: The student must correctly compute the speed just after leaving the net using energy or kinematics, obtaining 10 m/s.

title: Correct net force magnitude
description: Essential: The student must correctly apply the impulse-momentum theorem to find the constant net force magnitude, obtaining 1500 N.

title: Impulse-momentum setup
description: Important: The student must set up the impulse-momentum equation correctly, accounting for direction (signs) of velocities and including both the net force and gravity.

title: Consistent sign convention
description: Important: The solution must use a consistent sign convention for velocity and force directions throughout the calculation.

title: Includes gravity in force
description: Important: The student must recognize that the impulse equation involves the net force (F_net = F_net - mg) or explicitly account for gravity when solving for the force from the net.

title: Unit analysis or check
description: Optional: The student performs a unit check on the final force calculation or shows dimensional consistency.

title: Sign error in momentum change
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly handles the sign of the initial or final velocity in the impulse equation, e.g., treating both as positive without accounting for direction.

title: Omits gravity in force
description: Pitfall: The student solves for the force as if it were the net force alone, forgetting to add mg to find the actual force exerted by the net.
